metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Germany

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Germany using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name(s) (e.g., student design weights) or whether replicate weights were used for variance estimation, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Analysts using the OECD database should follow the PISA technical documentation and Reader’s Guide for the correct application of sampling weights and uncertainty estimation procedures when reproducing the reported means, shares, and correlations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than an empirical modeling paper that reports how plausible values (PVs) and missing data were handled in an ML pipeline. The outcomes shown (e.g., mean scores on a 60-point scale, proficiency level shares, and correlations/variance explained) are presented as OECD estimates, but the factsheet text does not describe PV generation/combining rules or missing-data procedures. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling details are not available in the provided excerpt and are treated as not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Germany is the set of 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science and for whom creative thinking results are reported in the Germany factsheet. The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions (e.g., missing questionnaire items, incomplete test forms) beyond the stated completion of the assessment; it reports 6116 students in 257 schools for Germany.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Germany’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Germany’s mean creative thinking score is 33 on a 60-point scale, which is on par with the OECD average. Germany also shows a relative pattern: students perform relatively higher on tasks requiring generating creative ideas and relatively higher in written and visual expression contexts, while struggling more with tasks combining social and scientific problems. The factsheet reports equity and perception-related associations (e.g., socio-economic status, gender gaps, and selected beliefs/attitudes) and notes COVID-19-related data collection challenges, with asterisks indicating countries/economies where PISA sampling standards were not fully met.
